name: Hotel Alfonso XIII
positioning: Hotel Alfonso XIII, a Luxury Collection Hotel: a Mudejar-style landmark commissioned by the King of Spain, in the Santa Cruz quarter next to the Reales Alcazares and Seville Cathedral
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to the Cathedral and the Reales Alcazares
Guests drawn to historic architecture and royal history

facts.text: The hotel was commissioned by the King of Spain to host international dignitaries during the 1929 Ibero-American Exhibition.
King Alfonso XIII inaugurated the hotel on 28 April 1928, and photographs of that day line the wall near the front desk.
The architect, Sevillian Jose Espiau y Munoz, was chosen through a competition.
The hotel is in the city center and the historic Santa Cruz quarter, right next to the Reales Alcazares and Seville Cathedral.
Guests have included Prince Rainier and Grace of Monaco, Prince Charles and Princess Diana, Ernest Hemingway, Orson Welles, Audrey Hepburn and Jackie Kennedy.
Bathrooms have marble floors and are tiled in characteristic Sevillian ceramic.
All suites have an independent living room that leads to the bedroom.
Grand Deluxe rooms with terrace are on the top floor.
Ena Sevilla is an outdoor terrace restaurant serving local tapas and wines, with views of the city center.
Bar Americano has an Art Deco style.
The concierge team are Les Clefs d'Or members.

highlights.text: The building has recessed ceramic friezes and a Mudejar style, a regional tradition inspired by Arab architecture.
The hotel has an outdoor swimming pool and gardens.
The Alfonso XIII Suite has a dining room for eight next to a kitchenette, with a chef available on request.
Restaurante San Fernando is in the colonnaded inner courtyard.
Serenity Retreat offers bespoke treatments, from massages to sensory rituals.

considerations.text: The Wellness Center is described as intimate.
The rooms do not have a work space.
